guarantees.claim: data_o is assigned SBOX_FWD[data_i] when op_i equals CIPH_FWD, SBOX_INV[data_i] when op_i equals CIPH_INV, and SBOX_FWD[data_i] for any other value of op_i.

assumptions.claim: SBOX_INV is a valid 256-entry array of 8-bit values accessible with data_i as an index.
assumptions.risk: If SBOX_INV is missing, incorrectly sized, or not defined in the same scope, a synthesis error or out-of-bounds access occurs, producing unknown data_o.

assumptions.claim: CIPH_FWD and CIPH_INV are module-level parameters with distinct values that correctly identify forward and inverse operations.
assumptions.risk: If CIPH_FWD == CIPH_INV, the inverse path is never taken and data_o always uses SBOX_FWD; if decoding is wrong, incorrect S-box is selected.

uncertain_points.claim: The else branch defaults to SBOX_FWD for any op_i value other than CIPH_FWD or CIPH_INV. This behavior may be unsafe if an unexpected op_i (e.g., from a fault or misconfiguration) occurs.
uncertain_points.cond: op_i is neither CIPH_FWD nor CIPH_INV
uncertain_points.risk: An invalid or fault-injected op_i forces the forward S-box lookup, possibly leaking decryption-quality output or enabling a cryptographic weakness; no error or fault is signaled.

uncertain_points.claim: The SBOX_INV array is used but not defined in this continuous region; its definition must be inspected to confirm it contains the correct inverse AES S-box values.
uncertain_points.risk: If the external definition of SBOX_INV is incorrect or mismatched with SBOX_FWD, the inverse substitution is wrong, breaking decryption without any local detection.
